concept.name: Percent B
concept.definition: A Bollinger-derived indicator expressing the close's position within the bands as a percentage of band width: 100 at the upper band, 0 at the lower band, 50 at the middle band, and beyond those values when price is outside the bands.
concept.intuition: %B states exactly where price sits inside the Bollinger envelope, making band tags, divergences and pattern confirmations quantifiable and comparable across securities.
concept.mechanics: Compute (Price - LowerBand) / (UpperBand - LowerBand) x 100 using the standard (20, 2) bands. Values above 100 mean closes above the upper band, below 0 below the lower band; used for walking-the-bands trend confirmation and W-bottom/M-top pattern work.
concept.formula: %B = ((P - LowerBand) / (UpperBand - LowerBand)) x 100, with bands from Bollinger Bands(20, 2) by default.
concept.failure_modes: Inherits the Bollinger SMA's lag, and readings above 100 can persist through an entire uptrend, so extremes are weak standalone timing signals.
concept.misconceptions: %B above 100 is not an automatic overbought-sell reading - upper-band tags in uptrends indicate strength; interpretation depends on trend and pattern context.
concept.example: Bands 47-53 with a close at 50: %B = (50-47)/(53-47) x 100 = 50; a close at 53.6 gives %B = 110.
